title: 🌏 Auckland Asian Networking Night
description:
Looking to meet new people, expand your professional network, or simply enjoy meaningful conversations over a drink?

Auckland Asian Networking Night is a relaxed community meetup inspired by Auckland's diverse Asian community, bringing together people from all backgrounds to connect, share experiences, and build genuine relationships.

You don't have to be Asian to join. If you enjoy meeting people from diverse backgrounds and appreciate Asian cultures, you're more than welcome.

No presentations. No formal agenda. Just good conversations.

👥 WHO'S THIS FOR?
Whether you're:

* A professional from any industry
* An entrepreneur or small business owner
* A freelancer or creative
* A student or working holiday maker
* Looking for a new career opportunity
* Or simply interested in meeting new people

💬 WHAT TO EXPECT
Grab a drink, introduce yourself, and join any conversation that interests you.

There's no fixed seating, no scheduled activities, and no pressure. Simply move around, meet different people, and enjoy conversations at your own pace.

You might leave with:

* New friends
* Professional connections
* Career insights
* Business opportunities
* Collaboration ideas
* Or simply a great evening with interesting people

Most people attend on their own, so don't worry if you're coming solo. We'll help you feel welcome.

📍 EVENT DETAILS

* Location: Mixed 1981 Cafe, 50 Fort St, Auckland CBD, Auckland
* Time: 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM (feel free to arrive a little earlier to grab a drink)
* Frequency: Every two weeks
* Capacity: Limited spaces available
* Entry: FREE for Hanahub members (Free to sign up at [hanahub.co.nz](https://www.hanahub.co.nz/))

☕ This event is proudly sponsored by Mixed 1981. All attendees are required to purchase at least one drink, and Hanahub members can enjoy 15% OFF food and drinks by showing their Hanahub member profile on the night.

🍪 Korean snacks will be served on the night, so come and enjoy a taste of Korea while you mingle.

title: Build Night: Demos, Collabs & Open Source in Practice
description:
A fortnightly, hands-on session focused on the projects the Auckland AI Collective is actually building — together.

Each session centres on **demonstrations** of what members are working on. Expect live demos, group experiments, and the occasional "let's just try it and see what happens" moment — so come ready to get involved, not just watch. Some parts may invite your participation; none of it is polished or precious.

The tone is **casual and informal**\- eat dinner\, drink\, and enjoy\. This is a place to share ideas\, get feedback\, find collaborators\, and turn "someone should build that" into an actual repo\.

What we cover will vary week to week depending on what people bring and what the group is curious about — the constant is the room: builders comparing notes and starting things together.

**This is for you if** you want to get directly and personally involved in group projects, collaborations, and **open source**.

See what we're already building on GitHub: [https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective](https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective)

Bring a project, a problem, an idea, or just yourself.

After this session we can hang out as long as we like at the restaurant if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

description:

title: Everyone's a Studio: Media, Culture and the Generation Era
description:
For a century, media meant pointing a camera or a microphone at something, and the cost of doing that decided what got made. That constraint is disappearing. Video, music, voices, 3D worlds and playable scenes can now be generated on demand, and captured reality itself is going volumetric: you can walk around inside a recorded moment.

This is a demo & discussion session: which trends are real, which are tech demos going nowhere, and what any of it does to society and culture. Bring your ideas and opinions.

We'll explore-

* The state of generation – video, image, music and voice: what's production-ready and what's still a party trick.
* From flat to volumetric – 3D, gaussian splats and 4DGS, explained plainly, and why they matter beyond the wow factor.
* Games and generated worlds – when environments, characters and story are made on the fly, what's left of a game as an authored thing?
* Entertainment for an audience of one – personalised media versus shared culture. What happens when nobody watched the same thing last night?
* Education – the infinitely patient tutor and the explainer built for exactly you, and whether anyone actually learns more.
* Who makes things now – production cost collapses. What that does to creative work, and who still gets paid.
* Trust and evidence – when any footage can be made, what counts as proof? Provenance, deepfakes, and the liar's dividend.
* The slop problem – infinite supply, finite attention. Do taste and curation become the scarce thing?

No prior background assumed. If you watch, play, make or teach, you have a stake in this.

Afterwards we usually continue over dinner nearby — a good chance to connect with fellow builders and practitioners.

title: When I Saw You (Jordan 2012) 1.30 mins
description:
We are in a season of films on Sunday afternoon about films about life in a war zone, especially Palestine.
I have chosen films that are not propaganda.
The attempt is to lift ourselves above that and do a deep dive into the realities of life in such areas. In this film, Tarek and his mother, Ghaydaa, cross the border from Palestine to Jordan along with tens of thousands of other people.

**When I Saw You** was selected at as the Palestinian entry for the best foreign language film at the Academy Awards. The New York Times reviewer wrote:
"A soft-centered child's-eye view of alienation, toughened by fine acting and Hlne Louvart's full-bodied photography."

The Total Film reviewer wrote: "political without point-scoring, Jacir remains true to a child's-eye view, with Asfa's delightful, exuberant performance always upfront."

"Palestinian filmmaker Annemarie Jacir's second film is slight yet significant - and, because of the situation in Syria, timely - story about a boy whose courage inspires hope among the hopeless."

A must-see for us all as we a look into the lives of familes fleeing from war - anywhere.
